articles.title: NI health: Further doctors' strike planned in ongoing pay dispute
articles.summary: Consultants and specialist doctors will begin a separate 24-hour strike on Monday morning as part of the same pay dispute.
articles.body:
A 24-hour strike by resident doctors in Northern Ireland is due to end at 07:00 GMT on Saturday.

But consultants and specialist doctors will begin a separate 24-hour strike on Monday, as part of the same pay dispute.

The British Medical Association (BMA) rejected a recommended 3.5% pay rise and wants to restore the value of doctors' pay to 2008 levels.

Health Minister, Robbie Butler, said he had accepted the recommended rise but could not implement it without sufficient funding for his department.

Friday's strike action by resident doctors affected non-emergency services, resulting in the cancellation of many planned outpatient appointments.

Urgent surgery and most GP services continued as normal because senior doctors remained on duty.

How will patients be affected on Monday?

Monday's walkout will involve consultants and specialty, associate specialist and specialist grade (SAS) doctors and will also take place over 24 hours from 07:00 on Monday.

Routine hospital and elective services are expected to be cancelled during the second strike.

But emergency care will continue under Christmas Day cover - which means full emergency cover will remain in place.

The Western and South Eastern health trusts have asked patients with appointments on Monday to attend as planned, unless their trust tells them otherwise.

The South Eastern Trust said the urgent care centre at Lagan Valley Hospital would be closed on Monday and that postponed appointments and procedures would be rescheduled as soon as possible.

Butler said more than 2,200 appointments were cancelled during similar strikes in June and warned the latest action would have "real consequences for patients, waiting lists and service delivery".

The BMA says years of below-inflation pay rises have made it harder for Northern Ireland's health service to recruit and retain doctors.

Dr Seamus Crumley, an anaesthetics registrar who works in intensive care at the Ulster Hospital, joined Friday's picket line in Belfast.

He told BBC News NI he had taken a pay cut when he moved from Scotland last year, despite securing a more senior role.

"The medical workforce here is very, very vulnerable to losing doctors to literally anywhere else in the UK, but also to the Republic of Ireland," he said.

Dr Steven Montgomery, who chairs the BMA's Northern Ireland Resident Doctors Committee, said his colleagues were facing burnout and emotional distress because of pressure at work.

He said the union was "not looking for this all to be paid in one lump sum" and wanted the minister to set out a plan to restore pay over time.

Dr Oisín Fearon, a resident doctor in Belfast, told BBC News NI he had considered moving to Australia, but family and local ties had kept him in Northern Ireland.

He said he had begun the process of registering to train in the Republic of Ireland and was keeping that option open.

Butler said he had met the BMA to explain the financial pressures facing his department and intended to implement the recommended award as soon as possible.

He said cumulative pay rises over the previous three years averaged 30% for resident doctors, 25% for SAS doctors and 24% for consultants.

Butler said the recommended rise was higher than that for other healthcare staff and warned that going beyond 3.5% would have "significant repercussions for nurses, teachers, police officers and indeed the entire public sector workforce".

Separately, the Northern Ireland Public Service Alliance (Nipsa) released the results of a recent ballot of its health and social care members.

It said 94% of its health and social care members backed strike action, while 97% backed action short of a strike, over growing pressures on the health and social care sector.

The union said it would consider its next steps and warned that coordinated industrial action could spread across the health service in the coming weeks.

articles.title: New drug combo shrinks tumors in most patients facing aggressive cancer type
articles.summary: The pancreatic cancer pill daraxonrasib shrank tumors in 60.7% of patients when paired with chemotherapy, and 8.2% saw tumors vanish on scans.
articles.body: Pairing an experimental pill with standard chemotherapy shrank tumors or halted growth in most patients with advanced pancreatic cancer, according to early clinical trial results presented Friday at a major international cancer conference. The findings, shared at the EORTC-NCI-AACR Symposium in Barcelona, come from a phase ½ trial testing a daily oral medication called daraxonrasib, along with two standard intravenous chemotherapy drugs, gemcitabine and nab-paclitaxel. The trial focused on 61 patients whose pancreatic cancer had already spread to other organs and who had not yet received treatment for their advanced disease. PANCREATIC CANCER PATIENT BEN SASSE SEES 'MASSIVE' TUMOR REDUCTION WITH EXPERIMENTAL NEW DRUG Pancreatic cancer is notoriously difficult to treat because more than half of patients are diagnosed after the disease has already spread, research shows. In major clinical trials for metastatic pancreatic cancer, chemotherapy alone shrinks tumors in about 23% to 42% of patients, but the disease typically begins growing again after five to six months, and most patients survive between 8 and 11 months. According to National Cancer Institute data, only about 3% of patients with distant-stage disease live five years past diagnosis. In the new study, which tracked patients for a median follow-up of 18 months, tumors shrank in 60.7% of cases, including 8.2% where they disappeared entirely on scans. Overall, the combination stopped tumor growth in 90.2% of participants. FDA APPROVES ONCE-DAILY PILL FOR DEADLY CANCER AFTER PATIENTS' SURVIVAL RATES NEARLY DOUBLE Patients went a median of 12.8 months before their cancer worsened, almost double the timeframe typically seen with standard chemotherapy, and 76.6% were still alive at the one-year mark, the study found. "We are now seeing not only substantial tumor shrinkages, including complete responses, but also durable disease control, with median progression-free survival exceeding one year," study lead Dr. Wungki Park, a gastrointestinal medical oncologist at Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center in New York, said in a press release. More than 90% of pancreatic cancers are driven by a faulty gene called RAS, which allows tumors to keep growing. Daraxonrasib is designed to turn off that growth signal, something scientists long thought was impossible to fix with medication. Dr. Elena Garralda, chair of the symposium and co-director of the clinical research program at the Vall d’Hebron Institute of Oncology in Spain, who was not involved in the research, said the results show that RAS-targeted drugs can be combined with existing treatments at the start of treatment to potentially achieve longer-lasting benefits. CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES Side effects included rash, diarrhea, fatigue and low blood cell counts linked to chemotherapy, most of which were manageable with standard care. Only 5% of patients stopped treatment because of side effects tied to daraxonrasib. TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ Researchers emphasized that the findings carry some limitations. Because this was an early-phase, single-group study involving 61 people, all participants received the experimental combination. Without a direct comparison group of patients receiving standard chemotherapy alone, doctors cannot yet confirm how much better the new regimen performs or whether it definitively extends overall survival. The findings also apply strictly to metastatic pancreatic cancer, even though RAS mutations drive several other cancers, including certain lung, colorectal and gynecological cancers. Separate studies would be needed to test whether the combination works in those diseases. CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER The trial was funded by Revolution Medicines, the California-based developer of daraxonrasib. articles.title: DR MARC SIEGEL: Cruise ships can be petri dishes for viruses. Calm may be the best cure
articles.summary: The CDC reports 148 aboard Princess Cruises' Caribbean Princess fell ill with stomach illness, as norovirus causes over 90% of cruise ship outbreaks.
articles.body: Fear is more contagious than any pathogen, especially on a cruise ship with a captive audience and a mysterious outbreak. As reported this week by Fox News Digital, "A Caribbean cruise has taken an uncomfortable turn for nearly 150 passengers and crew members who have fallen sick with stomach illness symptoms — with an infectious disease expert providing important insight into a very ‘common’ issue. A total of 148 people aboard Princess Cruises' Caribbean Princess — 134 passengers and 14 crew members — have reported the symptoms, according to the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)." The Caribbean Princess ship itself has since been replaced (2004), upgraded, and renovated (2019), but one thing remains unchanged: the propensity for infectious outbreaks aboard cruise ships, as well as the associated worry. Part of the problem on a cruise ship is the small, crowded quarters, the shared spaces, and the fact that seemingly no amount of disinfection is enough. Another problem is the delay in determining the actual pathogen, as is the case currently on the Caribbean Princess, where 148 people have now fallen sick with an unknown stomach illness. Even if there is nothing that can be done about it other than separation and increased disinfection, as is currently occurring on this ship, simply being able to put a name to the virus helps to calm fears. Cheap, rapid testing aided by artificial intelligence is in the future. Current rapid PCR testing on a ship the size of the Caribbean Princess takes dozens of expensive machines and many days to complete. It isn’t feasible. Norovirus causes over 90% of these outbreaks—about 10 to 20 per year, including one on this ship earlier this spring. The company has put out a statement about the cruise saying, "Princess Cruises can confirm that a limited number of guests aboard Caribbean Princess have reported mild gastrointestinal illness. Our crew responded promptly by implementing enhanced sanitation protocols across the ship, including comprehensive cleaning and disinfection measures. While most guests remain unaffected, we are continuing to closely monitor the situation." But sometimes a mysterious outbreak is due to something far worse than norovirus, where the delay in identification can cost lives. The MV Hondius embarked from Ushuaia, Argentina, on April 1, setting sail on a repositioning cruise offering a specialized ecotourism and research voyage. It was also unknowingly carrying the Andes strain of hantavirus, along with over 150 passengers and 57 crew. COULD HANTAVIRUS SPREAD ON A CRUISE SHIP? EXPERTS WEIGH RISKS AFTER DEADLY OUTBREAK This strain can spread human-to-human and can easily be deadly, especially when a person develops hantavirus pulmonary syndrome. One patient, Leo Schilperoord, developed a fever and flu-like symptoms on April 5, yet continued to mingle with passengers until April 10, when he died. A British birdwatcher became ill, and then, on April 22, Mirjam Schilperoord-Huisman developed symptoms. They were taken off the ship at the end of April and brought to Johannesburg, South Africa, for diagnosis and treatment. Finally, on May 1, 2026, when the ship’s doctor became ill, retired Oregon oncologist and dedicated birdwatcher Dr. Stephen Kornfeld took over. DR MARC SIEGEL, JENNIFER JOHNSON: MEET THE ANGEL DOCTORS FIGHTING HANTAVIRUS When I first interviewed Dr. Kornfeld for my new book, "The Angels Among Us," I was amazed to consider the ease with which he transitioned from a birdwatching role to putting his life on the line. But then I realized that it was simply a return to the same manner he’d developed for decades as a highly regarded and beloved oncologist in Oregon who calmed fears in the face of a patient’s uncertain future. As he said to me, the small group on that ship, which had by then traveled together for weeks and gone on many excursions, was like a family. "I know the limitations of equipment and medications on the ship. I know that if things become life-threatening for the sick people, my ability to intervene will be somewhat limited. At the same time, I know that I can just be reassuring to everyone on the boat, the crew, and the passengers. Letting them know that there is still a medical presence, that if other people get sick, there will at least be somebody to talk with them and try to help them. And I ultimately think this provides more of a service to the people on board than my actual care." DR MARC SIEGEL: HANTAVIRUS CRUISE OUTBREAK IS ALARMING, BUT FEAR IS SPREADING FASTER THAN FACTS Out there on the high seas, Kornfeld became an instrument of divine mercy, radiating a deep, spiritual strength that kept the frightened passengers from falling into total despair. By spreading calm, he slowed the spread of the virus, as people were far more capable of complying with restrictions and isolation. CLICK HERE FOR MORE FOX NEWS OPINION Finally, on May 4, it was determined in South Africa, where two patients were taken (Mirjam Schilperoord-Huisman ended up dying there), that this was the Andes strain of the hantavirus. Lengthy quarantines followed passengers disembarking in mid-May, and I visited the National Quarantine Center at the University of Nebraska Medical Center, where several patients were held in the same place I had once visited at the onset of the COVID pandemic. Overall, there were 13 reported cases and three deaths. Weeks later, it was finally confirmed that there was no spread beyond the 13 cases on the ship. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Travel on cruise ships can be relaxing and rejuvenating, especially if you are traveling to archipelagos otherwise unreachable. But when you are suddenly closed in with a threatening virus, whether it is a mild stomach bug or a deadly pulmonary virus, a ship can become a traveling petri dish—until an angel of healing like Stephen Kornfeld is sent by God to provide succor and thereby limit the spread. articles.title: Jennifer Aniston’s secret to staying fit at 57 starts with one simple workout routine
articles.summary: Jennifer Aniston trains three to four times a week with PVOLVE, and a trainer says consistency plus added weight training are key to her fitness success.
articles.body: At 57 years old, Jennifer Aniston seems to be defying the laws of aging — but it doesn’t come without hard work. The "Friends" actress has been public about practicing PVOLVE, a functional fitness method grounded in movement longevity. The workouts prioritize mobility and stability through twisting and reaching motions that translate directly to everyday life. Combining sculpting, cardio, and weight training, the method is designed to build muscle mass and support bone density. 10-MINUTE FITNESS HABIT CAN HELP ADULTS OVER 40 MAINTAIN MUSCLE AND STAY STRONG According to PVOLVE trainer Melanie Ramos, what keeps Aniston looking and feeling her best isn't a specific workout buzzword — it's consistency. "She's very consistent," Ramos told Fox News Digital. "She trains about three to four times a week doing PVOLVE, and she trains in all our modalities … She specifically is adding a lot more weight training into her routine." As people age, especially women, muscle mass begins to decline, according to Ramos, who serves as lead trainer at PVOLVE Soho in New York City. "So, I think for [Aniston], the consistency and just adding that extra weight training really helps her look amazing," she said. WANT TO AGE BETTER? RESEARCHERS SAY 4-MINUTE ROUTINE MAY HELP PREVENT DANGEROUS FALLS According to research published in the Journal of the American College of Cardiology, only about 20% of women regularly engage in strength training, with many opting for aerobic exercise instead. While walking offers major benefits for overall health, pairing cardio with simple resistance work can lead to significantly stronger heart and longevity outcomes. Rather than feeling pressured to commit to a full-hour workout to see results, Ramos advised simply getting started, adding, "Something that [Aniston] really prioritizes is even just getting 15 minutes of movement. " Starting with "baby steps" – aiming for at least three workouts per week, even if they're short – will help you feel "like you can achieve the goals you want," the trainer said. YOUR WALKING SPEED MAY HOLD A CLUE TO HOW LONG YOU’LL LIVE, STUDY SUGGESTS "And then build more of that lifestyle habit where it feels that you need that movement every day," Ramos continued. "Movement is a part of life, and as we age, we have to look at how we're moving our body." Prioritizing strength training and gradually increasing muscular load helps build lean mass and improve bone density, according to the trainer. articles.title: Biotech CEO says the US is fighting fentanyl ‘all wrong,’ urges new Democratic Congress to step up
articles.summary: Nearly a year after President Donald Trump designated illicit fentanyl a weapon of mass destruction, ARMR Sciences' CEO says treat it like a bioweapon.
articles.body: WASHINGTON — America is approaching the fentanyl crisis "all wrong" by waiting to reverse overdoses after they begin instead of blocking the drug with an experimental fentanyl vaccine, ARMR Sciences CEO Collin Gage told Fox News Digital. In an exclusive interview, Gage urged the new incoming Democrat-controlled Congress to build on President Donald Trump's designation of illicit fentanyl as a weapon of mass destruction and treat emerging synthetic drugs as a biodefense priority. ‘SUPER-DRUG’ 10 TIMES STRONGER THAN FENTANYL LINKED TO DEATHS ACROSS MULTIPLE STATES "If you look at the overdose crisis like any other health crisis, really as a disease, you'll know the best way to treat a crisis is by preventing it altogether," Gage said. "We need to completely overhaul the treatment paradigm and focus on preventing these deaths with new innovative therapeutics, rather than continuing the same approach that historically has led to tens of thousands of deaths, hundreds of thousands of deaths over the last several years." Why Gage calls synthetic drugs a 'unique biothreat' Gage pointed to President Donald Trump's designation of illicit fentanyl as a weapon of mass destruction as "absolutely critical" to shifting Washington toward a biodefense strategy. Gage says emerging synthetic drugs pose a distinct biological threat, unlike traditional chemical or biological weapons, because anyone can rapidly produce them using the dark web. "People often don't realize this, but fentanyl, carfentanil, nitazenes, medetomidine—all of these emerging synthetic drug threats are unique biothreats in that they're not like sarin gas, they're not like anthrax," Gage told Fox News Digital. "You can't go on the dark web and quickly formulate those substances. You can do that with these pharmaceutical-based agents that have completely caused havoc within the United States, and we're now starting to see that spread globally." 'ILLICIT' VERSION OF FENTANYL LINKED TO DEADLY NEW MEXICO INCIDENT THAT SICKENED FIRST RESPONDERS How a 'bulletproof vest' in the bloodstream could stop fentanyl ARMR Sciences is currently running a Phase 1/2 clinical trial to evaluate the safety of its experimental fentanyl vaccine and measure how effectively it blocks synthetic threats from reaching the brain. Rather than waiting for an overdose to begin, Gage explained how the technology works: EXCLUSIVE: INSIDE TRUMP'S CARTEL CRACKDOWN AS WHITE HOUSE OFFICIAL DETAILS PRESIDENT'S PRIVATE BRIEFINGS "We want our first responders to be as effective as they possibly can in the field," Gage said. PRESIDENT TRUMP’S DRUG CONTROL STRATEGY SETS THE PATH TO END THE DRUG CRISIS FOR GOOD A 'red, white and blue' push for the new Congress With a new Democrat-controlled Congress preparing to take office, Gage urged lawmakers to treat synthetic drug defense as a "red, white and blue" priority rather than a partisan issue, noting that fentanyl "does not discriminate" by race or socioeconomic status. Before expanding beyond the military to protect high-risk civilians like college students, Gage said safety and transparency must come first. GET BREAKING NEWS ALERTS ARMR Sciences publishes its full formulation on its website and intentionally left out heavy metals—a move Gage tied to Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr.'s push to scrutinize ingredients, while also praising former Rep. Patrick Kennedy's efforts to overhaul addiction treatment facilities. For Gage, whose mother struggled with addiction and who has lost friends to overdoses, the mission is deeply personal. FOLLOW US ON X "Passion is born from internal suffering," Gage said. "No family should look over and see an empty chair at the dinner table. No kid should be hiding in their room because they're scared if a parent is suffering from an addiction issue. I want to prevent that happening from any American across the country. articles.title: Estanislao Nistal, doctor en Virología: “Lo más probable es que el pico de la epidemia de gripe de este año se produzca entre finales de diciembre y febrero"
articles.standfirst: Nos enfrentamos a una temporada de gripe cargada de incertidumbre
articles.summary: Nos enfrentamos a una temporada de gripe cargada de incertidumbre
articles.body: Como cada año por estas fechas, empieza la preocupación por los virus y las enfermedades contagiosas, como la gripe. Esta es una enfermedad que siempre nos visita, cada año, y por ello debemos estar preparados para ese momento. Según refleja Estanislao Nistal, doctor en Virología, para este año se espera que “el pico de la epidemia de gripe se produzca entre finales de diciembre y febrero". Y, para ello, menciona que una de las estrategias más sencillas y eficaces es la vacunación no solo para prevenir y sortear las infecciones respiratorias, sino para reducir el impacto que causa la enfermedad en caso de infectarnos. El farmacéutico Joaquín López, menciona la importancia de estar preparados para tratar los síntomas cuando llega la gripe a nuestro entorno lo antes posible. Para ello, recomienda "tener en el botiquín de casa medicamentos antigripales que nos permitan aliviar nuestros síntomas de manera conjunta". Según un estudio elaborado por Kantar para Kimberly-Clark, solo el 5,4% de los españoles se abastece con los productos idóneos para aliviar los síntomas de la gripe y los resfriados. Para el especialista existen ciertas medicinas que podemos incorporar en nuestro botiquín para paliar los síntomas de la gripe estacional y pasar un invierno más calmado. Aunque es importante que seamos conscientes de que no es recomendable consumir medicamentos sin receta médica, sí que es importante tener en el botiquín de nuestros hogares algunos medicamentos que nos ayuden a mitigar los síntomas de la gripe estacional. Uno de ellos es el paracetamol, el cual actúa frente al dolor y a la fiebre, pero también están el dextrometorfano; para calmar la tos seca, la pseudoefedrina; para la congestión nasal, la cafeína; para combatir el decaimiento, la clorfenamina; ideal para la secreción nasal y los estornudos; y la vitamina C para ayudar al funcionamiento normal de tus defensas naturales. Por otro lado, el especialista menciona que no solo es importante tratar los síntomas, sino un abordaje precoz el virus para mejorar el bienestar del paciente durante el proceso y ayudar a disminuir la propagación de los agentes infecciosos. Si sabemos que estamos contagiados, por ejemplo, cuando tosamos y estornudemos, habría que cubrirse correctamente para que haya menos posibilidades de que contagiemos a los que nos rodean. En cualquier caso, ante la aparición de síntomas compatibles con alguna infección respiratoria, es recomendable consultar con un profesional sanitario para que pueda valorar la situación que tenemos de manera individual y concreta, además de aplicar el tratamiento que considere óptimo para nuestro caso.

articles.body: Thiruvananthapuram: Govt will not adopt an approach of blaming doctors for every issue, said health minister K Muraleedharan on Saturday. He assured the medical fraternity that financial constraints wouldn’t affect the healthcare sector.Addressing a function marking the platinum jubilee celebrations of Thiruvananthapuram Medical College Alumni Association, Muraleedharan said chief minister V D Satheesan, who also holds the finance portfolio, had assured that the healthcare sector wouldn’t be affected by the state’s financial difficulties.Govt will soon create more doctor posts to reduce the workload of existing medical staff, he said. Those heading hospitals should also give special attention to maintaining cleanliness and ensuring proper disinfection of hospital premises, he added.“Doctors are the saviours for ordinary patients. Medical science is evolving rapidly, and doctors must keep pace with changing technology while retaining compassion towards patients,” he said.The minister said Thiruvananthapuram medical college had provided relief to lakhs of people over the past 75 years. “Its growth is closely linked to the development of the state’s public healthcare system. It is a matter of pride that several doctors who had studied at the institution are now serving in different parts of the world,” he said.Doctors at the medical college played a significant role in ensuring quality treatment for ordinary people, he added.Muraleedharan appreciated the alumni association’s initiative to construct an amenity centre at a cost of Rs 15 crore. He said the association was taking valuable suggestions from doctors and called for discussions on the institution’s growth over the next 25 years.The minister released a coffee-table book, documenting the history of modern medicine and the growth of Thiruvananthapuram Medical College. He also released the alumni association’s platinum jubilee souvenir and presented awards to doctors who had made contributions in various fields.Stay updated with the latest Thiruvananthapuram news. articles.title: Grand Theft Auto VI mania could endanger marriages as relationship coach exposes red flag
articles.summary: Couples jump into Grand Theft Auto VI's release as relationship expert Matthew Hussey of Los Angeles shares advice on balancing gaming passion with real relationships.
articles.body: The long-awaited arrival of Grand Theft Auto (GTA) VI has become a craze among gamers, and a point of contention between couples. Ahead of the video game’s release on Nov. 19, couples on social media anticipated how the game might create space in their relationships — with users posting about men gearing up for hours of gameplay and women worrying about the resulting distance. While some posted videos of men gifting their partners flowers and treats ahead of the download, others took a firmer stance on prioritizing gameplay over relationship time. 'GRAND THEFT AUTO VI' MANIA COMES WITH SERIOUS HEALTH RISKS, DOCTORS WARN One husband jokingly created a contract where his wife signed in agreement of 10 days of uninterrupted play, allowing requests "at my convenience." The husband also reminded his wife that everything in the game is fictional. Grand Theft Auto VI has drawn scrutiny from regulators and commentators for its heightened mature content, which includes strong sexual themes, nudity, strip club missions and satirical references to an in-game adult subscription brand modeled after OnlyFans. Those elements are among the features most concerning to spouses, according to social posts. When gaming interferes Relationship coach, podcaster and author Matthew Hussey weighed in on how couples can avoid letting GTA VI negatively affect their relationships. The Los Angeles-based expert acknowledged that it’s a "real problem" if a video game results in a partner not having their needs met. WHY COUPLES SHOULD FLIRT WITH EACH OTHER EVERY DAY — PLUS THE ‘RED FLAG’ TO AVOID Hussey noted that there are worse habits people can have, like staying out late drinking every night, although gaming does have the potential to become addictive. In most cases, a new, exciting game release is a special interest and a passion that should be supported by one's partner, according to the expert. Hussey argued that gaming deserves the same respect from partners as any other hobby, such as practicing jiu-jitsu, playing golf or going to the movies, rather than being treated as something to shame. "If we know GTA 6 is about to come out, and it's really important to them, and they've been looking forward to it, we should be the ones saying, 'How do we carve out more time for you this week to go and play? Because I know this is a big moment for you,'" he said. THE MARRIAGE WARNING SIGN THAT MAY BE WORSE THAN FIGHTING — AND 4 WAYS TO TURN THINGS AROUND While it's healthy to support a partner’s hobby, it shouldn't come at the expense of the relationship, Hussey noted. "If you're suddenly at a point where you're like, 'I'm not getting my needs met, and I literally am coming second to this video game all the time,' then that's a real conversation [that needs to be had]," he said. While sexually explicit gameplay can cause friction for some couples, Hussey called it "interesting," comparing it to reading popular, steamy "romantasy" novels. "If my wife was reading a romance novel, and she was fantasizing things that she was reading in that book, I don't mind. It's a book, it's fantasy," he said. "I think the reverse argument might be made in some ways for GTA VI, where it's not living in the world of reality." TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ Hussey cautioned that interactions in a game should not become a "surrogate" for the real thing, pulling one partner away from a real-life relationship. "[If] you're doing things for a character in a game, like you haven't texted your wife back, but you are worried about texting your character girlfriend back ... that's a different story, and I think that's a real problem." The expert said he’s more worried about single people who don’t have a partner who can "call them out" if they’re spending too much time in a fictional reality. "There's no one there to ring the alarm and say, 'You're on your 14th night in the house, and you haven't interacted with a real person or given yourself a real shot at finding love,'" he said. CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER "I think video games are awesome. … We're just going to have to be really disciplined about asking ourselves, 'Am I still investing in real relationships or has this become a surrogate for them?'" Talking to a partner about excessive gaming Bringing up unmet needs caused by excessive gaming can be difficult for couples. Hussey suggests starting not with criticism, but by showing you have your partner’s best interests at heart. It's important to clarify that you aren't trying to take away a hobby they love, and instead are framing it around your own needs, he added. "Somewhere in the process you're starting to feel overlooked, and there are things that are important to you that you don't feel like you're getting," he said. CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS "If you show someone ... that you genuinely care about their happiness and them getting their needs met … they're not seeing someone who's at odds with them," he went on. "It's not an antagonistic conversation. It's someone looking at you as their teammate." CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Framing the conversation this way encourages reciprocity, Hussey said, prompting a partner to think, "I better get my act together, because this isn't a given that I would have a partner who's this supportive of me."

articles.title: Cura de aplasia de medula: menina encontra doadora em Curitiba | G1
articles.standfirst: Aos 8 anos, Noemi reencontrou Geovania, que se cadastrou como doadora voluntária de medula óssea em 2011 e foi compatível com a menina, que passou pelo transplante em 2023, em Curitiba.
articles.summary: A pequena Noemi, que viajou da Bahia ao Paraná para tratar uma aplasia de medula óssea, celebrou a cura em um emocionante reencontro com sua doadora voluntária.
articles.body:
Aos oito anos, Noemi Lima reencontrou, em Curitiba , a mulher que doou a medula óssea responsável por salvar sua vida. As duas foram reunidas durante a consulta em que a menina, natural da Bahia, recebeu a confirmação da cura, quase cinco anos depois de enfrentar o diagnóstico de aplasia de medula óssea e passar pelo transplante no Hospital Erastinho, na capital paranaense.

Para Noemi, a doadora Geovania Oliveira Santos é uma heroína.

"Pra mim ela é uma salvadora de vida, uma super-heroína", diz a menina.

🔎 A aplasia de medula óssea é uma doença rara em que a medula deixa de produzir células sanguíneas em quantidade suficiente, comprometendo a produção de glóbulos vermelhos, glóbulos brancos e plaquetas.

Noemi Lima e a doadora Geovania Oliveira Santos — Foto: Reprodução/RPC

Noemi tinha dois anos quando começou a apresentar manchas esverdeadas na pele. Inicialmente, ela foi diagnosticada com púrpura — condição caracterizada pelo aparecimento de manchas na pele causadas por pequenos sangramentos sob a superfície. A menina começou a tomar corticoides, mas precisou ser levada à emergência.

"Aí a gente foi pra emergência. As plaquetas estavam muito baixas e, então, colocou a gente na regulação, pra ver onde interná-la", contou a mãe.

Foi durante essa trajetória que Geovania entrou na história da família. Técnica de enfermagem, ela se tornou a doadora compatível que possibilitou o transplante.

"É muito importante esse momento, porque você não salva só o paciente, você salva a vida da família inteira", disse Geovania.

Noemi Lima, no início do tratamento, e Geovania Oliveira Santos realizando a doação — Foto: Reprodução/RPC

Doação aproximou famílias de diferentes estados

A mãe, Juliana Silva Oliveira, conta que a família precisou buscar atendimento especializado até conseguir a transferência para Curitiba.

Para confirmar o diagnóstico e iniciar o tratamento, os pais e a menina deixaram Feira de Santana , na Bahia, e se mudaram para a capital paranaense.

Segundo a médica Antonella Zanette, chefe do serviço de transplante de medula óssea do Hospital Erastinho, a Bahia não contava com transplante de medula óssea pediátrico.

"A Noemi tinha muito anticorpo, então a gente teve que esperar mais um pouco pra realmente conseguir um doador 100% compatível e sem anticorpo, pro risco de perder a medula ser menor", explicou.

O transplante foi realizado em 2023, pelo Sistema Único de Saúde (SUS).

Noemi Lima e a médica Antonella Zanette — Foto: Reprodução/RPC

Família deixou a Bahia para acompanhar tratamento

Para os pais, a notícia trouxe alívio, mas também medo diante de um procedimento que ainda era desconhecido pela família.

"Foi um alívio e um medo, porque o transplante pra mim era um caminho que a gente não conhecia", lembra a mãe.

O pai, Fábio Lima Oliveira, conta que a mudança para Curitiba exigiu deixar a rotina e os planos para trás. A família fez diversas viagens entre a Bahia e o Paraná durante o tratamento.

Noemi Lima e os pais recebendo a notícia de cura da médica Antonella Zanette — Foto: Reprodução/RPC

Entre consultas, internações e idas e vindas, Noemi cresceu. Quase cinco anos depois do diagnóstico, a família voltou a Curitiba para uma consulta especial: a confirmação da cura.

O pai conta que uma das lembranças mais emocionantes foi quando comprou uma bicicleta para a filha. Na época, ele pensava que ela ainda teria muitas oportunidades de brincar e aproveitar a infância.

"Um mês mais ou menos que a gente comprou outra bicicleta maior. E aquilo pra mim foi muito emocionante", contou.

Agora, com a confirmação da cura, Noemi pode explorar o mundo com mais tranquilidade.

A menina Noemi Lima cresceu durante o tratamento — Foto: Reprodução/RPC

A história da menina só teve esse desfecho porque Geovania se cadastrou voluntariamente no Registro Nacional de Doadores de Medula Óssea (Redome).

Técnica de enfermagem, ela fez o cadastro em 2011, depois de uma doação de sangue no Ceará. Anos depois, foi identificada como compatível com Noemi e realizou a doação.

Para Geovania, o reencontro e a confirmação da cura representam a dimensão do gesto.

Pessoas entre 18 e 35 anos, em bom estado de saúde, podem fazer o pré-cadastro para se tornar doadoras voluntárias de medula óssea. Depois, é necessário finalizar o processo no hemocentro mais próximo.

A doação pode ser realizada até os 60 anos de idade.

articles.title: VÍDEO: Cliente joga ventilador contra caixa em São Vicente | G1
articles.standfirst: A agressão aconteceu em São Vicente (SP) após a funcionária pedir ao filho da cliente que guardasse brinquedos. A vítima procurou atendimento médico.
articles.summary: Vítima afirma ter sido xingada e agredida após pedir para o filho da cliente organizar brinquedos que ele havia tirado de uma prateleira.
articles.body:
Uma operadora de caixa de 31 anos foi agredida por uma cliente em uma loja de variedades em São Vicente , no litoral de São Paulo. Imagens obtidas pelo g1 mostram o momento em que a mulher empurra a funcionária e joga um ventilador contra ela ( assista acima ).

O caso aconteceu na Avenida Prefeito José Monteiro, no Jardim Independência, na tarde deste sábado (21). A vítima, que preferiu não se identificar, contou ao g1 que a confusão começou após ela pedir ao filho da cliente que organizasse os brinquedos de uma prateleira.

Segundo a funcionária, uma colega de trabalho a orientou a pedir ao menino que guardasse os brinquedos após manuseá-los. "Eu falei assim: 'Ei, menino, depois que você achar o que está procurando, junta tudo e guarda, tá bom? Não deixa no meio do corredor'", afirmou.

Segundo a funcionária, a mãe não gostou da abordagem e disse que o menino "tinha mãe" e "não era criança de rua". A operadora de caixa afirmou que não gritou com a criança e tentou explicar o motivo do pedido. Ela também destacou que sabe lidar com crianças, pois tem uma filha de 9 anos.

De acordo com a funcionária, antes de sair da loja, a cliente a xingou e fez ameaças. Ela então decidiu tirar uma foto da placa do carro da mulher após ela deixar o estabelecimento.

Ao perceber a ação, a cliente retornou à loja, xingou novamente e empurrou a funcionária. Segundo a vítima, a mulher jogou contra ela um ventilador que estava ligado à tomada, arranhou seus braços e rosto e tentou tomar o celular de sua mão.

A operadora de caixa pediu para a cliente esperar a chegada da polícia, mas a mulher foi embora. "Quero ver a polícia vir atrás de mim", teria dito a cliente, segundo a vítima. O g1 não conseguiu localizar a mulher para ouvir sua versão até a última atualização desta reportagem.

Cliente agride funcionária em loja em São Vicente (SP) — Foto: Arquivo pessoal

A funcionária contou que ficou abalada após a agressão, chorou e precisou procurar atendimento médico. Ela foi por conta própria ao Hospital São José, onde, segundo seu relato, uma médica constatou que sua pressão arterial estava alta. A vítima também afirmou que bateu a região das costelas, sentia fortes dores e realizou exame de corpo de delito.

Ela explicou que já estava com febre desde quinta-feira (19) devido a um tratamento para infecção urinária. Por estar debilitada, afirmou que não teve forças para reagir e tentou apenas se defender. A funcionária também disse que preferiu não revidar devido à diferença física entre as duas, já que mede 1,54 metro, enquanto a cliente teria cerca de 1,80 metro.

Ventilador ficou quebrado após a agressão — Foto: Arquivo pessoal

A operadora de caixa afirmou que está com medo e ansiedade. Ela relatou que foi a primeira vez que passou por uma situação como essa, tanto na vida quanto durante o ano em que trabalha na loja.

"Estou indignada [...] E foi covardia o jeito que ela veio para cima de mim. Eu poderia ter batido a cabeça. [...] Eu quero justiça. Que ela não faça isso com ninguém, e que, antes de agir assim, ela pense que não está [lidando] com um animal. Nenhum animal merece isso. Isso não se faz com ninguém", destacou.

Vítima teve ferimentos leves nos dois braços e no rosto — Foto: Arquivo pessoal

Segundo a vítima, a mulher já frequentava a loja e costumava agir com rispidez, além de deixar os filhos circularem sozinhos pelo estabelecimento. A operadora de caixa afirmou, porém, que a cliente não apresentava comportamento agressivo quando entrou na loja neste sábado.

A funcionária ainda não havia registrado boletim de ocorrência, mas afirmou que pretende procurar a polícia.

Cliente agride funcionária em loja em São Vicente (SP) — Foto: Reprodução

articles.title: Mulher que perdeu casa em enchente de 2024 é atingida por tempestade | G1
articles.standfirst: Dalva de Oliveira conta que se mudou para cidade atingida por chuva devastadora após perder tudo em Estrela, cidade que foi atingida pela força da água há dois anos.
articles.summary: Dalva de Oliveira conta que se mudou para cidade atingida por chuva devastadora após perder tudo em Estrela, cidade que foi atingida pela força da água há dois anos.
articles.body:
Uma moradora que teve a casa atingida pela tempestade em Tupanciretã na madrugada desta sexta-feira (20) já havia passado por outra situação trágica há dois anos , quando a casa em que ela morava em Estrela foi destruída pela enchente que atingiu a região do Vale do Taquari , no Rio Grande do Sul, em 2024.

"Quase morri chorando. Tenho depressão por tudo que passei em Estrela, e agora estou abalada", conta Dalva de Oliveira.

Um rastro de destruição foi deixado no município de 20 mil habitantes, que foi atingido por uma supercélula com indícios microexplosão e ventos de 114 km/h na madrugada de sexta-feira (20).

Segundo a moradora, ela e o marido, que tem problemas cardíacos, precisaram se abrigar no banheiro da casa durante a tempestade . Os vidros da casa foram quebrados e uma parede da residência está instável por causa da força do vento.

De acordo com a última atualização da Defesa Civil do RS, cinco pessoas morreram na cidade após a passagem da tempestade . Mais de 24 mil pessoas foram afetadas e 36 cidades registraram estragos . Ainda há 162 feridos e mais de 20 mil pessoas fora de casa . Ao todo, 8,5 mil residências tiveram danos.

Moradora de Tupanciretã perdeu a casa durante enchente de 2024 — Foto: Reprodução/RBS TV

Vítima estava internada no Hospital São Vicente de Paulo, em Cruz Alta. Morte foi confirmada na tarde deste sábado (21).

Vítima estava internada no hospital desde a sexta-feira (20).

O idoso foi socorrido ao hospital de Júlio de Castilho s, cidade vizinha de Tupanciretã, mas não resistiu aos ferimentos. Segundo relato de uma familiar, a casa onde ele morava desabou durante o temporal.

A mulher estava em casa, acompanhada da nora, quando a residência foi destruída pelo temporal . Hortência não resistiu aos ferimentos e faleceu antes da chegada do socorro. A nora ficou presa nos escombros, mas posteriormente foi socorrida e passa bem.

A neta Ethyane Alves lamentou a morte da avó: "Era uma pessoa incrível, alto astral, adorava estar com a família e sempre preocupada com todos".

Ex-vereador de Tupanciretã, Ronaldo foi eleito como vereador em Tupanciretã por sete mandatos : em 2020, 2016, 2012, 2008, 2004, 2000 e 1992. A morte foi confirmada pelo presidente estadual do PSDB, Moisés Barboza.

"Ronaldo dedicou parte de sua trajetória à vida pública e ao trabalho em favor da comunidade de Tupanciretã, deixando sua contribuição à história política do município e do nosso partido", disse Barboza.

Tempestade com vento e granizo deixa rastro de destruição em Tupanciretã — Foto: Amanda Boeira/Grupo RBS

O Centro de Monitoramento da Defesa Civil do RS analisou imagens e vídeos da tempestade que atingiu Tupanciretã na madrugada desta sexta-feira. Há indícios de que a cidade tenha sido atingida por uma microexplosão . Uma estação do Instituto Nacional de Meteorologia (Inmet) registrou rajadas de vento de 114 km/h durante o temporal.

"Até o momento, não é possível confirmar a ocorrência de um tornado no município. As evidências apontam para ventos severos associados à supercélula, possivelmente provocados por uma microexplosão. A possibilidade de tornado não está completamente descartada, mas o fenômeno, isoladamente, não explicaria a extensão dos danos registrados na cidade", destaca a Defesa Civil.

Os dados do radar meteorológico de Porto Alegre indicam a atuação da supercélula por volta das 3h19.

A Defesa Civil do RS emitiu, às 2h38, um alerta vermelho por SMS para a região, incluindo Tupanciretã, indicando risco de granizo grande e vendaval, com risco muito alto de destelhamentos. O alerta teve vigência até as 3h37.

Tempestade causa uma morte, deixa feridos e atinge quase todas as casas de Tupanciretã — Foto: Arte g1

articles.title: Gêmeos passam por cirurgia inédita a laser ainda no útero em MT | G1
articles.standfirst: Cirurgia foi feita em Cuiabá para tratar uma complicação que poderia levar à morte dos bebês. Segundo médico, não há registro de outro procedimento do tipo no estado.
articles.summary: Cirurgia foi feita em Cuiabá para tratar uma complicação que poderia levar à morte dos bebês. Segundo médico, não há registro de outro procedimento do tipo no estado.
articles.body:
Gêmeos passam por cirurgia inédita a laser ainda no útero em Mato Grosso — Foto: Hospital Geral e Maternidade de Cuiabá

Dois bebês que ainda estavam na barriga da mãe passaram por uma cirurgia a laser em Cuiabá para tratar uma complicação que poderia provocar a morte dos dois. O procedimento foi realizado pelo médico Maurício Saito, no Hospital Geral e Maternidade de Cuiabá , na segunda-feira (16), e, segundo o médico Morales Fernando M. Leite, responsável pelo acompanhamento da gestação, é o primeiro desse tipo com registro encontrado pela equipe em Mato Grosso.

A cirurgia foi indicada para tratar a síndrome da transfusão feto-fetal , uma complicação que pode ocorrer em gestações de gêmeos que compartilham a mesma placenta. A doença provoca uma passagem desigual de sangue entre os bebês: um recebe menos sangue do que precisa, enquanto o outro recebe em excesso.

Morales acompanhou a intervenção por meio de exames de ultrassom e orientou a equipe durante a cirurgia. Maurício Saito é especialista em medicina fetal e veio de São Paulo para realizar o procedimento.

A síndrome foi diagnosticada quando a gestação estava com 19 semanas. No dia da intervenção, a mãe estava com 23 semanas e três dias. Segundo Morales, a doença havia avançado para o estágio 2, com risco de provocar a morte dos bebês ou deixar sequelas.

Por um pequeno acesso na barriga da mãe, os médicos introduziram uma câmera para visualizar a placenta e identificar as conexões anormais entre os vasos sanguíneos. Com um laser, o especialista fechou essas ligações para interromper a passagem desequilibrada de sangue entre os bebês.

Durante o procedimento, também foi retirado o excesso de líquido que se acumulava ao redor de um deles. Segundo Morales, a cirurgia contou com equipes de anestesia e com a estrutura do hospital para atender a mãe e os bebês caso houvesse alguma complicação.

Na avaliação feita cerca de 24 horas depois, os dois bebês apresentavam movimentos e oxigenação dentro da normalidade. O líquido ao redor do bebê que estava em menor quantidade havia voltado ao nível considerado normal. Já o excesso de líquido do outro não havia voltado a se acumular após a drenagem.

“Cerca de um dia depois do procedimento, nós reavaliamos com o ultrassom. Os bebês já estavam um pouco melhores, bem ativos, com toda a oxigenação normal”, afirmou.

A mãe também apresentou boa recuperação e recebeu alta no dia seguinte à cirurgia. Apesar da evolução inicial favorável, o acompanhamento médico continua. Segundo Morales, as primeiras 72 horas após a intervenção são consideradas um período de maior risco. Uma nova avaliação foi programada para esse intervalo, seguida de outro exame após uma semana. Se a gestação permanecer estável, o acompanhamento poderá passar a ser feito a cada 15 dias.

Procedimento ainda não é realizado regularmente

Segundo Morales, a cirurgia exige treinamento específico e equipamentos próprios. Atualmente, Mato Grosso não conta com profissional capacitado para realizar esse tipo de intervenção de forma regular. Por isso, pacientes que precisam do tratamento costumam ser encaminhadas para centros especializados de outros estados.

No caso atendido em Cuiabá, a equipe conseguiu trazer o especialista e os equipamentos necessários para realizar o procedimento no hospital. Segundo o médico, a unidade ofereceu estrutura e profissionais para dar suporte à mãe e aos bebês, inclusive em caso de necessidade de cuidados intensivos.

“O Hospital Geral tem uma estrutura, equipe que consegue dar o suporte para esse procedimento, como foi o caso que aconteceu. Então essa cirurgia ainda não é disponibilizada de forma regular”, explicou.

O médico disse que a equipe pesquisou registros de cirurgias semelhantes em hospitais de Mato Grosso e não encontrou casos anteriores. Outras intervenções em bebês ainda no útero já foram realizadas no estado, mas por meio de cirurgia aberta, com abertura do útero da mãe. No caso dos gêmeos, o tratamento foi feito por fetoscopia, técnica que permite visualizar e operar a placenta com uma câmera e instrumentos introduzidos por um pequeno acesso.

Morales afirmou que a equipe pretende buscar parcerias para viabilizar novos procedimentos no estado quando houver indicação médica. Por enquanto, segundo ele, a técnica não é oferecida de forma regular em Mato Grosso.

O procedimento foi realizado pelo médico Maurício Saito, no Hospital Geral e Maternidade de Cuiabá, na segunda-feira (16) — Foto: Hospital Geral e Maternidade de Cuiabá

articles.title: Nelson Massini lança livro sobre casos de Zuzu Angel e Mengele | G1
articles.standfirst: 'O Corpo Não Mente', de Nelson Massini e Paolla Serra, reúne histórias de mais de cinco décadas da atuação do legista na Medicina Legal, incluindo o acidente com césio-137. Lançamento será no dia 26 de novembro, em Ipanema.
articles.summary: Em 'O Corpo Não Mente', Nelson Massini e Paolla Serra detalham investigações de casos históricos da medicina legal, como o acidente com césio-137 e mortes na ditadura.
articles.body:
Legista e jornalista lançam livro com bastidores de casos históricos no Rio — Foto: Divulgação

O médico legista Nelson Massini, que participou de investigações de mortes que marcaram a história do Brasil e de outros países, lança no dia 26 de novembro, no Rio de Janeiro, o livro O Corpo Não Mente, escrito em parceria com a jornalista e advogada Paolla Serra.

A obra reúne bastidores de casos como as mortes da estilista Zuzu Angel, do guerrilheiro Carlos Lamarca, do líder seringueiro Chico Mendes e do nazista Josef Mengele.

“Este não é apenas um livro sobre crimes. É um livro sobre o papel da perícia, que pode fazer justiça a quem sofreu violência ou impedir que um inocente seja condenado”, afirma o legista.

Publicado pela Editora Máquina de Livros, o livro apresenta relatos de mais de cinco décadas de atuação de Massini na Medicina Legal. Em primeira pessoa, o legista conta como exames periciais ajudaram a confrontar versões oficiais, esclarecer circunstâncias de mortes e revelar detalhes que não apareciam em depoimentos e documentos.

Um dos episódios abordados é a morte de Zuzu Angel, em 1976. A estilista morreu depois que seu carro, um Karmann-Ghia, caiu do Viaduto Mestre Manoel, em São Conrado, na Zona Sul do Rio. Em 1997, a pedido da família, Massini reanalisou o caso e encontrou depoimentos de testemunhas que relataram a presença de outros veículos próximos ao automóvel antes da queda.

Zuzu Angel morreu quando seu carro caiu da Estrada da Gávea, na saída do Túnel Dois Irmãos, no Rio de Janeiro — Foto: TV Globo/Reprodução

Tempos depois de entregar o parecer, o legista comprou um Karmann-Ghia TC, do mesmo modelo. Segundo ele, dirigir o carro permitiu compreender melhor suas dimensões, a resposta ao volante e o comportamento do veículo em uma manobra abrupta.

Caso do césio-137 e amizade com menina vítima da radiação

Outro episódio lembrado no livro é o acidente radiológico com césio-137, em Goiânia, em 1987. Massini integrou a equipe responsável pelos exames das vítimas e acompanhou o caso de Leide das Neves Ferreira, de 6 anos, uma das vítimas mais jovens da tragédia.

A menina havia manipulado o pó radioativo e depois comido pão com ovo com as mãos contaminadas. Durante o período em que esteve internada no Hospital Naval Marcílio Dias, no Rio, ela e o legista desenvolveram uma amizade.

Leide morreu em decorrência de uma hemorragia causada pela radiação, e a mesma equipe que a acompanhou precisou realizar o exame após sua morte.

Massini também relembra a repercussão de um episódio envolvendo o transporte dos corpos das vítimas, que precisaram ser acondicionados em mantas de chumbo. A operação levou cerca de quatro horas por corpo.

Na época, um cortejo de caixões atravessou as avenidas Presidente Vargas e Rio Branco, no Centro do Rio, em direção ao Aeroporto Santos Dumont. A aeronave, porém, aguardava na Base Aérea do Galeão. A situação rendeu manchetes na imprensa popular, com referências a um suposto desfile do legista com o césio pelo Centro.

No livro, Massini contesta essa versão. Segundo ele, houve um erro de percurso provocado pelo cansaço e pela desinformação, e as medições realizadas afastavam riscos à população.

De Mengele ao massacre de Eldorado dos Carajás

A obra também reúne episódios de repercussão nacional e internacional. Entre eles, a investigação sobre a morte do nazista Josef Mengele, que viveu escondido no interior de São Paulo, e a análise das mortes de 19 trabalhadores rurais durante o massacre de Eldorado dos Carajás, no Pará, em 1996.

Em outro capítulo, Massini aborda a morte de Carlos Marighella. Segundo a análise apresentada pelo legista, o guerrilheiro não teria caído no banco traseiro de um Fusca depois de ser atingido por tiros. Seu corpo teria sido colocado no veículo.

O livro também revisita a morte do engenheiro Raul Amaro Nin Ferreira, em 1971. Aos 27 anos, ele foi preso durante uma ação da ditadura militar, passou pelo DOI-Codi e terminou internado no Hospital Central do Exército, onde morreu.

Em 2014, Massini examinou o caso com base em um relatório produzido pelos sobrinhos de Raul e publicado pela Editora PUC-Rio.

Entre os episódios mais recentes está a morte da publicitária Juliana Marins, no vulcão Rinjani, na Indonésia, em 2025, acompanhada em tempo real por brasileiros.

Para Massini, a perícia tem papel fundamental na investigação de crimes e na responsabilização de envolvidos.

Legista Nelson Massini e jornalista Paolla Serra — Foto: Divulgação

A jornalista e advogada Paolla Serra, coautora da obra, conheceu Massini há cerca de 20 anos, quando ele era fonte de suas reportagens. Com o tempo, os dois se tornaram amigos e decidiram reunir as histórias em livro.

Com experiência em grandes coberturas policiais e autora de "Caso Henry: Morte anunciada", Paolla ficou responsável por transformar os relatos técnicos, laudos e procedimentos da Medicina Legal em uma narrativa acessível ao público.

“Muitas vezes, não encontramos a resposta nos depoimentos, nos processos ou nas declarações de autoridades. Ela está nos corpos”, afirma a jornalista.

Lançamento no Rio: 26 de novembro, às 19h

Local: Livraria da Travessa de Ipanema- Rua Visconde de Pirajá, 572, Ipanema, Zona Sul do Rio.

O livro também terá lançamento em Brasília, no dia 1º de dezembro, na Platô Livraria.

articles.title: Hibernation for longevity: Woman diagnosed with first case of ‘hibernation syndrome’ every winter for 30 years could hold clues to human longevity
articles.summary: Imagine if the secret to living a longer, healthier life wasn’t about eating better or working harder, but simply slowing your body down.
articles.body: Imagine if the secret to living a longer, healthier life wasn’t about eating better or working harder, but simply slowing your body down. That’s exactly what scientists started thinking after hearing about one woman from the Netherlands.As reported by The Sun, for more than 30 years, each winter, her body shifted into a strange hibernation-like state. Her temperature dropped way below normal, to about 31°C, and she moved in slow motion. It wasn’t just feeling groggy because of the cold; her body genuinely operated as if conserving energy for survival. What’s wild is that, despite these yearly deep freezes, she recovered each time fully and showed no obvious signs of organ damage.What happened to the woman who appeared to hibernate every winter?Doctors first noticed this odd pattern in her early 20s. She died at 57, but not due to her mysterious winter syndrome. Instead, it was complications after an unsuccessful surgery for pneumonia, which is a completely separate issue. Before her death, she agreed to donate her brain to science, giving researchers a unique opportunity to see what was happening inside her head. When they finally examined her brain, they stumbled upon clues that might explain how a human body could tolerate such profound changes, and what it might mean for the rest of us.The findings were published in Neuropathology and Applied Neurobiology and caught the attention of plenty of curious scientists. There’s still no miracle lifespan treatment, but suddenly, researchers are wondering whether we humans have some hidden ability to turn down our metabolism and conserve energy, just like bears or squirrels do when they hibernate. Who knows, maybe one day doctors could use this knowledge to help patients survive longer during critical illness or even help astronauts endure those never-ending space missions.How did this woman actually ‘hibernate’?The research team, led by Chun-Xia Yi from Amsterdam University Medical Centre, first encountered her case while sifting through donated brains, especially focusing on the hypothalamus, that tiny part of your brain that acts like mission control for everything from temperature to metabolism and sleep.Over the years, her medical record told a consistent story. Every winter, she slowed down and became oddly lethargic. Doctors measured her body temperature during these episodes and found it was just 31°C, which is dangerously low compared to the usual 37°C. But this wasn’t just oversleeping or the winter blues. Animals in hibernation dramatically lower their metabolic rate and temperature to survive cold, foodless months. This woman’s condition mimicked some of those features, though scientists felt it was most accurate to call her state ‘hibernation-like’. For years, everything seemed normal in her MRI scans, even at age 55. But after her death, the donated brain revealed some unusual findings at the molecular level.What did the scientists find?Turns out, her hypothalamus was pretty different. The most notable change was in a protein called synaptophysin, which helps neurons communicate. Compared to other women her age, she had only about one-tenth as much synaptophysin in the hypothalamus. That means fewer neural connections in the regions that manage body temperature and our natural sleep-wake rhythm.Researchers also found that two critical signaling substances: arginine vasopressin (regulates water balance and other functions) and vasoactive intestinal peptide (helps manage biological rhythms) were unusually low. Combined, these findings point to a hypothalamus that operates differently, maybe making it possible for her body to enter a super-energy-saving mode every winter.Is there any limitation?However, there’s a big unknown here. Scientists can’t say for sure whether these brain changes triggered her hibernation-like states, or if the states caused the brain changes. They published even more findings, showing changes in immune markers and neurons, while noting the brain’s basic structure stayed intact.Could humans someday ‘hibernate’ to live longer or survive extreme situations?That’s the big question. Humans obviously don’t hibernate seasonally as animals do, but maybe there’s some hidden biological switch we could learn to turn on under certain circumstances.The potential uses are pretty exciting. For instance, doctors could possibly help critically ill patients hang on longer while awaiting transplants by dialing down their metabolism. Astronauts heading out on epic missions might someday use hibernation tricks to conserve food and resources.Researchers are now combing through the woman’s genome, hunting for unique genetic variations that could explain her rare ability. If they uncover specific pathways, it might be possible to recreate similar effects through medical intervention in the future.Still, it’s important to set expectations straight. There’s no proof that lowering a human’s body temperature or inducing hypothermia extends life. In reality, hypothermia is dangerous, as it can wreck your heart, nervous system, and organs. Early reports show other cases of “human torpor,” but none lasted as long or provided access to brain tissue for deep study. As Matteo Cerri, a University of Bologna researcher, notes, this woman’s decades-long experience sets her story apart.As of now, science is just scratching the surface. Understanding how the human body manages its internal clock, metabolism, and energy use could one day lead to breakthroughs for survival medicine or space travel. Right now, we don’t have the formula for longevity. But this case cracks open a door: maybe slowing down, rather than speeding up, is one way to help us live, especially when survival is on the line.Get the latest movie news, reviews, and celebrity updates. articles.title: NEIGRIHMS trains hosp administrators in emergency preparedness
articles.summary: NEIGRIHMS held a 6-day emergency preparedness training for 38 hospital administrators from five northeast states, with modules and hospital visits in Shillong.
articles.body: Shillong: The North Eastern Indira Gandhi Regional Institute of Health and Medical Sciences (NEIGRIHMS) conducted a six-day training programme on hospital preparedness for health emergencies for hospital administrators from across the northeast.Organised under the aegis of the disaster management cell of the Union ministry of health and family welfare, the programme was held from Nov 16 to 21.Thirty-eight participants from Manipur, Meghalaya, Mizoram, Nagaland and Tripura attended the training.“The participants were trained in different modules on disaster management, including onsite visit to two tertiary care hospitals in Shillong (NEIGRIHMS and Nazareth Hospital). Resource persons from different agencies and parts of the region were involved,” a NEIGRIHMS statement said.“Due diligence in managing emergency cases on a day-to-day basis in our hospitals serve as the best drill towards preparedness for handling mass casualties, and hence each one of us should endeavor to manage trauma and other emergency cases efficiently and in a timely manner,” NEIGRIHMS director Prof. Nalin Mehta said.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Guwahati | Silver Rate in Guwahati | Bank Holidays in Guwahati | Public Holidays in Guwahati | Guwahati AQI | Weather in Guwahati | Petrol Price in Guwahati | Diesel Price in Guwahati | CNG Price in Guwahati | LPG Price in GuwahatiStay updated with the latest Guwahati news.
